Hi all,

Quick answers and evidence pointers below — happy to jump on a technical call with FinBank security to walk through live architecture and demo BYOK flow.

1) HSM support / customer-managed keys:
- We do not host customer-owned HSM appliances inside our environment. For HSM-backed keys we rely on cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) which offer HSM-backed key storage. Customers can bring their own keys by creating keys in their cloud KMS and granting Redwood's service principal (least-privilege IAM role) access for cryptographic operations.
- In short: BYOK via customer cloud KMS (HSM-backed by provider) is supported. We do not accept customer physical HSMs installed inside Redwood-managed infrastructure.

2) Key rotation and availability:
- Customers can rotate keys on their schedule in their KMS. Recommended pattern: create a new key version/alias in your KMS, update the Redwood key alias binding (we support seamless alias updates), and do a controlled rolling update.
- Our runtime uses a short-lived cache for encryption keys (and per-tenant KV caching for inference). The system supports atomic key alias swaps and graceful fallback to previous key for in-flight requests to avoid downtime. We also recommend coordinating a brief rolling restart of inference workers for high-throughput long-running workloads; in practice most rotations are completed without visible interruption.

3) GDPR / revocation:
- Revocation: Since keys for BYOK are provisioned in the customer's KMS, customers can revoke access at any time (revoke the service principal or rotate to a new key). We will confirm any data-access actions with the customer and provide the audit evidence.
- We provide full audit logging for key usage (KMS request IDs and timestamps) that can be attached to GDPR/Data Subject Access Request (DSAR) evidence packages.

4) Evidence and artifacts I am attaching to this thread:
- redwood_SOC2_report_2025.pdf (redacted where required)

- Small architecture diagram showing where keys live and call flows
